commands.review_summary:
The branch adds WhatsApp Web outbound USync PN-to-LID discovery, trusted-contact token diagnostics, reachout-timelock early errors, socket adapter methods, and focused send-api tests.

PR surface: Source +314, Tests +85. Total +399 across 4 files.

Reproducibility: Partly. Source inspection shows current main lacks these token/timelock diagnostics, and dependency-source inspection shows the PR's new USync path will not request LID data for phone users; I did not reproduce the live cold-contact WhatsApp failure.

target.title: add whatsapp outbound token diagnostics
target.body:
## Summary

Improves diagnostics for proactive WhatsApp Web 1:1 sends to contacts that may not have an existing conversation with the account.

Practically, this targets a failure mode where OpenClaw/Baileys reports a message as sent, but WhatsApp never actually delivers it to the recipient. This can happen with new WhatsApp numbers or cold 1:1 conversations when WhatsApp requires trusted-contact token state or has an active reachout timelock.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can currently look successful when WhatsApp Web is not actually able to deliver a proactive 1:1 message to a cold contact.

That is bad operationally because the agent may believe a message was sent while the recipient never receives it. This PR makes that state visible and actionable:

- it attempts USync before sending to discover and persist PN/LID mappings
- it checks trusted-contact token state for direct 1:1 sends
- it logs useful diagnostics when the token is missing
- it throws a clear error before `sendMessage` when reachout timelock is active

## Behavior

- resolves phone-number targets to LID via USync when possible
- persists forward and reverse LID mapping files in the auth dir
- checks the `tctoken` store before direct 1:1 message sends
- logs missing trusted-contact token diagnostics
- fails early when reachout timelock is active, instead of letting the send look accepted while WhatsApp never actually delivers it

## Evidence

Focused validation run locally from the PR branch:

```text
$ pnpm tsgo:test:extensions
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/extensions-test.tsbuildinfo
# exit code 0
```

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.extension-whatsapp.config.ts whatsapp/src/inbound/send-api.test.ts
Test Files  1 passed (1)
Tests       41 passed (41)
```

The focused send-api tests cover the important behavior paths:

- existing authDir PN-to-LID mapping is used for sendMessage
- USync lookup can discover a LID and persist forward/reverse mapping files before sendMessage
- active reachout timelock without trusted-contact token fails before sendMessage
- missing token diagnostics do not block when reachout timelock is inactive
- existing fallback PN routing still works when no LID mapping exists
- poll, reaction, and composing sends still resolve PN-to-LID through the existing LID-aware path
